Institutional setting

Modern facility exterior; architecture and daylight signal scale and credibility.

Laboratory precision

Cool, high-contrast lab imagery; blue gloves and dark background support a clinical technology tone.

Device on neutral field

White-grey gradients let the blue catheter silhouette and magenta particles read clearly.

Molecular science

Small colored molecular forms against white, with magenta heading accents and indigo labels.

Coating close-up

Translucent materials, magnification rings and particles explain the coating without visual clutter.

Arterial navigation

Saturated red tissue contrasts with the silver-blue device and pale callout panels.

Drug transfer

Luminous particles and close vascular geometry communicate the transfer process.

Packaging finish

Grey seamless studio, glossy floor reflections and small color accents keep the product range premium.

SUPPLIED SUPPORTING REFERENCE · NOT A VIDEO FRAME

Balloon folding / sectional validation graphic

The separately supplied scientific figure compares a balloon section, numerical prediction and superimposition, with a 1 mm scale. It may guide a technical explanation of fold geometry or validation, but it should only be inserted into the advertisement if the team has permission to use it and can confirm it depicts the same device/design and validated method.

04 / Production notes

Editorial, audio & visual consistency

Practical direction for reproducing or revising the film in 3D, compositing and motion graphics.

Camera & animation

Use slow, deliberate product orbits and precise macro moves. Keep the catheter’s orientation consistent between product renders and internal vessel shots. Use controlled zooms to bridge the full device, balloon folds and sectional mechanism.

Typography & graphic system

Use a modern sans-serif, compact section headings and short callout bars. Reserve magenta for headings/product cues, indigo for technology labels, and white translucent panels for text over red vessel environments. Protect legibility on 1080p.

Music & sound design

The supplied storyboard specifies a soft background track. Keep it understated beneath narration; use restrained transitions or subtle technical accents only where they help explain the mechanism. Avoid sensational heartbeats or alarm-like effects.

Modeling & materials

Device: translucent pale balloon, blue guidewire/shaft, controlled specular highlights. Tissue: warm red/pink layers with enough separation to identify wall and lumen. Drug particles should be visible but not resemble debris or uncontrolled loss.

Motion-graphics priorities

Animate in causal order: process → balloon inflation/contact → drug transfer → tissue movement. Callouts should appear near the relevant component, hold long enough to read, and clear before the next mechanism begins.

End-frame discipline

Keep the product hero, Protégé name, certification artwork and Translumina end slate crisp. Do not recolor official logos or certification marks. Match package artwork and product-variant names to approved design files.

Clinical / regulatory review: This storyboard organises claims found in the supplied video and script workbook; it does not independently validate them. Before external use, review statements about paclitaxel, absorption/retention, positive vessel remodelling, drug loss, multiple inflations, therapeutic dosage, Protégé NC market-positioning, and safety/efficacy against current approved labeling, substantiation and jurisdiction-specific requirements. Keep the wording aligned with the approved IFU and legal/regulatory review.
